videos.title: How Reversible Reactions Approach Equilibrium | Year 12 Chemistry
videos.description:
Explain why the forward reaction slows and the reverse reaction speeds up as a sealed flask approaches dynamic equilibrium. Follow phosphorus pentachloride splitting and re-forming, read concentration and rate graphs, then predict what changes when the flask starts with only products.

Chemistry 2017: Year 12 Module 5, Equilibrium and Acid Reactions. Supports explaining how changing reactant and product concentrations affect reaction rates on the way to equilibrium.
Syllabus dotpoint (NSW Chemistry Stage 6, 2017, Module 5):
"investigate the relationship between collision theory and reaction rate in order to analyse chemical equilibrium reactions"
Official 2017 course: https://www.nsw.gov.au/education-and-training/nesa/curriculum/science/chemistry-stage-6-2017

Prerequisite: Static and dynamic equilibrium, reversible reactions and equal opposing rates in a closed system. Next: How an equilibrium responds to concentration and temperature changes.

videos.title: External and Internal Fertilisation: Why Egg Numbers Differ | Year 12 Biology
videos.description:
Explain how external and internal fertilisation bring sperm and egg together, and why water, timing and protection matter. Compare coral, salmon, frogs, hens and seals to connect egg numbers and parental care to offspring survival. Build a short exam answer and distinguish where fertilisation happens from where the young develop.

Biology 2017: Year 12 Module 5, Heredity. Supports analysing mechanisms of sexual reproduction in animals that ensure continuity of a species.

Syllabus dotpoint (NSW Biology Stage 6, 2017, Module 5):
"explain the mechanisms of reproduction that ensure the continuity of a species, by analysing sexual and asexual methods of reproduction in a variety of organisms, including but not limited to:
- animals: advantages of external and internal fertilisation"
Official 2017 course: https://www.nsw.gov.au/education-and-training/nesa/curriculum/science/biology-stage-6-2017

Prerequisite: Sexual and asexual reproduction, gametes and why offspring must survive for a species to continue. Next: How plants reproduce, followed by fungi and microbes.
